name: Cyberdesk

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Not a compute rental: Cyberdesk hosts no VMs. Customers install the Cyberdriver agent on their OWN physical or virtual Windows machines; Cyberdesk bills per automation step (agentic steps and cheaper cached/replayed steps) at contract-specific rates. Steps are billed for success, user-task-failed and cancelled runs; infrastructure failures are not billed. No per-vCPU/GiB/hour rate exists, so rates stay null.

caveats: Public desktop automation API product with demo-led sales; /pricing renders only headline even in Chrome. No verified hosted OS hardware size, tariff or CPU-hour rate. Windows desktop use is lead evidence, not guaranteed purchasable Windows VM configuration.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Cyberdesk is a computer-use AGENT platform, not a machine host: every machine is customer-supplied (Cyberdriver on your own Windows PC/VM), billed per agentic/cached step at contract rates; no public price, self-serve is a waitlist. Any Windows VM cost is paid separately to the customer's own cloud. Consider excluding it from compute rankings or keeping the mode 'alt' with all rates null.
API rate limits: dashboard JWT traffic 480 requests/user and 4,000 requests/org per 60-second window; public API-key limits separate and unpublished; raise by emailing the founders.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Provision Windows: Use Windows Server 2022 or a supported Windows desktop environment. RDP is useful for initial setup, but Cyberdriver should continue working after RDP disconnects.
snapshot_auto.note: Cyberdesk hosts no machines. You provision your own Windows PC/VM and install Cyberdriver (a RustDesk-based tunnel agent). Machine lifecycle and snapshots belong to your own cloud or hypervisor.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: The Cyberdriver CLI is useful when you bake a Windows AMI or golden template, then clone many VMs from it. The main rule is simple: install Cyberdriver in the image, but connect each cloned VM with its own API key and identity when it first boots.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No first-party snapshot API. Golden images and AMIs are made in your own cloud. The docs' 'trajectories' (recorded action replays) and 'workflow duplication' are not machine snapshots.

own_agent_api.quote: This guide will walk you through creating your first workflow, installing Cyberdriver, and executing a run programmatically.
own_agent_api.note: Cyberdesk's own computer-use agent only. The REST API plus TS/Python SDKs let you create runs (workflow prompt plus inputs, per-run prompt/model overrides), bulk runs, run chains on a reserved machine session, retry, get run messages/screenshots/attachments, and receive run_complete webhooks. The agent runs in Cyberdesk's cloud and drives the desktop through the Cyberdriver tunnel, not inside the machine. No token streaming or third-party harnesses (Claude Code, Codex) documented.

harness_api.quote: This guide will walk you through creating your first workflow, installing Cyberdriver, and executing a run programmatically.
harness_api.note: Cyberdesk's own computer-use agent only. The REST API plus TS/Python SDKs let you create runs (workflow prompt plus inputs, per-run prompt/model overrides), bulk runs, run chains on a reserved machine session, retry, get run messages/screenshots/attachments, and receive run_complete webhooks. The agent runs in Cyberdesk's cloud and drives the desktop through the Cyberdriver tunnel, not inside the machine. No token streaming or third-party harnesses (Claude Code, Codex) documented.

egress_allowlist.quote: Cyberdriver connects outbound to Cyberdesk over HTTPS/WebSocket. Some organizations need that traffic to go through a company-controlled domain for firewall allowlisting or traffic inspection.
egress_allowlist.note: The machine and its network are yours. Egress control is your own firewall or cloud security groups. Cyberdesk offers no per-machine egress policy, only guidance on routing Cyberdriver's own tunnel through your proxy.

egress_http_rules.note: Not a machine host. No first-party network policy of any kind.

guest_firewall.note: Your own Windows machine with Administrator (the installer requires admin), so Windows Defender Firewall / netsh rules apply. nftables/iptables don't apply (Windows).

secret_proxy.quote: Sensitive values are stored in a secure vault during the run, never logged or sent to LLMs, resolved only during actual computer actions, and deleted immediately after the run completes.
secret_proxy.note: Sensitive inputs and desktop parameters ({$password}, stored in Basis Theory) are hidden from the LLM and logs but are typed or used on the desktop itself, so the secret does enter the machine. Not an outbound credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Use Windows Server 2022 or a supported Windows desktop environment.
volume_attach.note: No hosted machines, so no first-party volumes. Disks are whatever your own VM/PC has. Files move via the file read/write API and run attachments.

volume_shared.quote: Use Windows Server 2022 or a supported Windows desktop environment. RDP is useful for initial setup, but Cyberdriver should continue working after RDP disconnects.
volume_shared.note: Cyberdesk hosts no machines at all: automation runs on the customer's own physical or virtual Windows PC, reached via the Cyberdriver tunnel agent. There is no first-party disk/volume of any kind (see volume_attach:false, same evidence), so a shared-volume-across-sandboxes feature cannot exist either. Docs, API reference (machines/pools/workflows), and llms.txt index show no volume or shared-storage concept; files move only via run attachments and signed-URL file read/write, not mounted storage. Confirmed as 'no'.

image_oci.quote: The Cyberdriver CLI is useful when you bake a Windows AMI or golden template, then clone many VMs from it.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cyberdesk is a Windows desktop-automation agent platform with no machine provisioning API; there is no Docker/OCI image concept, only customer-made Windows AMIs/golden templates in the customer's own cloud.

docker_inside.quote: Cyberdesk is an AI-powered desktop automation platform built for real-world software operations... across Windows desktops and virtual machines.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cyberdesk automates existing Windows desktop/VM software via screenshots, mouse, keyboard, and PowerShell; it does not provide or manage a container runtime.

nested_virt.quote: Cyberdesk is an AI-powered desktop automation platform built for real-world software operations... across Windows desktops and virtual machines.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No hosted compute means no notion of nested virtualization inside a Cyberdesk-provided machine.

desktop.quote: Desktop Tools is the dashboard control surface for a connected Cyberdriver machine. It sends requests through Cyberdesk's authenticated tunnel to the local Cyberdriver service... Take screenshots... Move the cursor... Type text...
desktop.note: Graphical desktop access/streaming is provided via the RustDesk-based Cyberdriver tunnel, but the desktop itself is the customer's own Windows machine, not one hosted by Cyberdesk.

browser.quote: It helps teams automate repetitive and high-stakes work across Windows desktops and virtual machines, including legacy applications, EHR systems, ERP interfaces, and browser-based workflows.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cyberdesk automates whatever browser is already installed on the customer's own Windows machine; it does not provide or manage a first-party browser instance.

anti_bot.quote: Cyberdesk is an AI-powered desktop automation platform built for real-world software operations.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cyberdesk is a desktop/UI automation agent for internal business software (EHR/ERP/legacy apps), not a web-scraping/stealth-browsing product; no fingerprinting or bot-detection evasion is documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Cyberdesk is an AI-powered desktop automation platform built for real-world software operations.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving capability is documented anywhere in the docs or product pages.

ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Remote access/control is via the Cyberdriver RustDesk-based tunnel (screenshots/mouse/keyboard) and a PowerShell shell endpoint, not SSH.

snapshot.quote: The Cyberdriver CLI is useful when you bake a Windows AMI or golden template, then clone many VMs from it. The main rule is simple: install Cyberdriver in the image, but connect each cloned VM with its own API key and identity when it first boots.
snapshot.note: No first-party snapshot API. Golden images/AMIs are made in the customer's own cloud; Cyberdesk's 'trajectories' are recorded UI-action replays, not machine memory/disk snapshots.

fork.quote: The Cyberdriver CLI is useful when you bake a Windows AMI or golden template, then clone many VMs from it. The main rule is simple: install Cyberdriver in the image, but connect each cloned VM with its own API key and identity when it first boots.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cloning a Windows AMI/template is done entirely in the customer's own cloud (e.g. AWS); Cyberdesk has no machine-cloning API of its own.

fork_running.quote: install Cyberdriver in the image, but connect each cloned VM with its own API key and identity when it first boots.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No machine host, so no fork capability of any kind.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: install Cyberdriver in the image, but connect each cloned VM with its own API key and identity when it first boots.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No snapshot or fork feature exists, so memory-preserving fork does not apply.

pause_resume.quote: Cyberdesk is an AI-powered desktop automation platform built for real-world software operations.
pause_resume.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cyberdesk does not control the lifecycle of the customer's machine at all, so it cannot pause/resume it or its billing (billing is per automation step, not per machine-hour).

wake_on_request.quote: Keep local and remote desktop sessions active while idle
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cyberdriver's Keepalive feature prevents the customer's own Windows machine from going idle/sleeping; Cyberdesk has no capability to power on or wake a stopped machine on request.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Keep local and remote desktop sessions active while idle
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; the documented idle behavior is the opposite (Keepalive keeps the customer's machine active during idle periods). Cyberdesk does not stop/sleep customer machines since it does not own their lifecycle.

persistent_disk.quote: Cyberdesk is an AI-powered desktop automation platform built for real-world software operations.
persistent_disk.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Disk persistence is a property of the customer's own PC/VM, not something Cyberdesk provides or manages.

live_resize.quote: Use Windows Server 2022 or a supported Windows desktop environment.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cyberdesk does not allocate or resize CPU/RAM for any machine; sizing is entirely the customer's own VM/PC configuration.

agent_harnesses.quote: This guide will walk you through creating your first workflow, installing Cyberdriver, and executing a run programmatically.
agent_harnesses.note: Cyberdesk only offers its own computer-use workflow agent (via prompts, trajectories, and the runs API); no third-party coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) are documented as preinstalled or offered as templates.

lang_python.quote: pip install cyberdesk / poetry add cyberdesk / pipenv install cyberdesk
lang_python.note: First-party Python SDK for driving the Cyberdesk API (creating/managing runs, workflows), documented with async/sync examples.

lang_node.quote: npm install cyberdesk / yarn add cyberdesk / pnpm add cyberdesk ... Node.js 18+ or another runtime with fetch support
lang_node.note: First-party TypeScript/Node.js SDK for driving the Cyberdesk API.

public_ipv4.quote: Cyberdriver connects outbound to Cyberdesk over HTTPS/WebSocket.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cyberdesk provides no machine and thus no IP address of any kind; the customer's own PC/VM has whatever addressing its own network provides.

inbound_https.quote: Cyberdriver connects outbound to Cyberdesk over HTTPS/WebSocket. Some organizations need that traffic to go through a company-controlled domain for firewall allowlisting or traffic inspection.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The Cyberdriver agent only makes outbound connections to Cyberdesk; there is no Cyberdesk-provided inbound HTTPS URL to reach ports on the customer's machine.

ingress_rules.quote: Cyberdriver connects outbound to Cyberdesk over HTTPS/WebSocket.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. There is no Cyberdesk-managed network surface to which ingress rules could apply.

static_egress_ip.quote: Cyberdriver connects outbound to Cyberdesk over HTTPS/WebSocket. Some organizations need that traffic to go through a company-controlled domain for firewall allowlisting or traffic inspection.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Outbound IP is whatever the customer's own machine/network has; Cyberdesk offers only guidance on routing the Cyberdriver tunnel through the customer's own proxy, not a Cyberdesk-provided fixed egress IP.

gpu.quote: Cyberdesk is an AI-powered desktop automation platform built for real-world software operations. It helps teams automate repetitive and high-stakes work across Windows desktops and virtual machines.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cyberdesk hosts no compute of any kind, so no GPU machines are offered by Cyberdesk itself (any GPU is the customer's own hardware).

macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cyberdesk/Cyberdriver targets Windows machines only; no macOS client or support is documented.

arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope for the stated product. The published Cyberdriver installer is windows-x64 only; no ARM64 build is documented.

self_host.quote: Cyberdesk provides: A REST API at https://api.cyberdesk.io / Official TypeScript and Python SDKs
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The Cyberdesk backend (dashboard, workflow engine, API) is a hosted SaaS at api.cyberdesk.io; only the Cyberdriver client agent installs on the customer's own machine, no self-hosted backend is documented.

open_source.note: Cyberdriver client binaries are distributed via a GitHub releases page, but no OSI license or public source code for the core Cyberdesk platform/agent was found; treated as not open source.

max_session_h.quote: While a session is active, that machine is dedicated to your session only... Exclusive access to one machine for the session's duration (strong scheduling guarantee)
max_session_h.note: Cyberdesk does not host the machine and does not document any maximum duration for a session/reservation or for the underlying Windows machine, which is the customer's own and runs until they stop it; no Cyberdesk-imposed session time limit was found.

mcp_server.quote: API Reference: Complete reference for all Cyberdesk API endpoints
mcp_server.note: Cyberdesk's integration surface is documented as a REST API plus TypeScript/Python SDKs and Zapier/Slack webhook integrations; no MCP server is listed in the docs index, on cyberdesk.io, or among the cyberdesk-hq GitHub org's public repos (cyberdesk, cyberdriver, cyberdriver-new, cyberdriver-server, starter kits) as of 2026-09-30.
